title: Reading Drill — Estimating the age of painted boards — A pilot study
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Estimating the age of painted boards — A pilot study
passages.body:
**A** A project in Millcross began with reports of later paint coats looking older than earlier repairs. The paint conservator had heard several complaints, but individual reports could not show how often the problem occurred. The team collected evidence using detailed photographs and chose the number of distinct paint layers as its main measure. That allowed it to compare different days using the same rule.

**B** The proposed response was comparison of protected edges. Rather than apply it immediately across the whole site, the team ran a trial in a single area. The trial lasted six weeks. A second area kept its previous arrangements, making it possible to see whether any change occurred at both sites.

**C** The first review recorded exposure to direct light as a factor that could affect the comparison. The team advised repeating the study under different conditions before drawing a wider conclusion. It kept the evidence from the first trial but published a note about why the figures might not apply elsewhere.
